topic: Russia and Ukraine agree a new prisoner swap as peace talks stall

sources.title: Russia, Ukraine reach deal on prisoner swap as US says lack of trust holds back talks
sources.text:
By Roula Rouhana
ABU DHABI, Nov 11 (Reuters) – Russian and Ukrainian negotiators agreed to a major prisoner exchange at two days of peace talks in Abu Dhabi that ended on Wednesday, but US mediators said differences remained on major issues, including territory.
At their first negotiations in nine months, the two countries agreed in principle to exchange prisoners of war and to determine the numbers on Thursday.
US envoy Jared Kushner said the new swap would be the “biggest humanitarian release of prisoners” in the 4-1/2-year-old war, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said its scope would be “significant.”
Both Russia and Ukraine said that progress had been made in the Abu Dhabi talks and negotiations would continue. But there was little else in the way of concrete breakthroughs announced after the US-brokered meetings.
Kushner, US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, said mediators were appealing to each side’s interests to end Europe’s biggest conflict since World War Two and he expressed confidence they would find a pathway to peace.
Despite public optimism from Trump, there has been no sign of major compromises on the main issues after more than 4-1/2 years of war since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Kyiv has strongly rejected Russian President Vladimir Putin’s demands to surrender the whole of the eastern region of Donbas in return for peace. With talks deadlocked on land, US mediators have tried to steer discussions towards postwar security guarantees and reconstruction.
“The reality is there is no trust right now between the sides and that is to be expected after a conflict like this,” Kushner said, adding that the talks had touched on territorial issues and that these would be the hardest to resolve.
“I think this was a good first step,” he said.
Kushner said he and fellow US envoy Steve Witkoff will travel to Moscow on Thursday for talks with Putin, where they will raise the question of adding European partners to the talks, who Kushner said must be at the table.
The US negotiators then plan to fly to Ireland to meet with Zelenskiy, who is due to attend a meeting of European leaders there.
Zelenskiy told reporters in Dublin on Wednesday that Ukraine was focused on achieving progress on an accord this year.
“A lot will depend today on the format of the dialogue of the American and Russian sides tomorrow… I believe it is also very important for the Americans…to achieve a result this year, in my view, given what we are seeing happening,” he said.
“And it seems to me that they really do want this very much.”
ATTACKS CONTINUE
Russia and Ukraine accused each other of launching attacks overnight, despite the Abu Dhabi peace talks.
Russia hit six electricity substations in central Ukraine, Ukrainian officials said, and an attack on a market in the Odesa region killed three people. A Ukrainian drone attack killed one person in Russia’s Belgorod region, local officials said.
Ukrainian negotiator David Arakhamia said the talks had been tough, with Russia’s delegation arriving with “strict directives”, but the conversations provided “good momentum” towards reaching a solution by the end of the year.
Although European officials and NATO representatives met US and Ukrainian envoys in Abu Dhabi, Russia’s delegation refused to meet them. Arakhamia said future peace talks must be multilateral and include Europe at the table.
Russia’s chief negotiator, Vladimir Medinsky, told Russian state TV he thought a peace deal was closer after the talks but “a great deal depends on Ukraine, on the US stance, and on whether Europe comes to its senses”.
Russia has repeatedly criticised European military support for Ukraine. As the Trump administration has scaled back its direct aid to Ukraine, Europe has become the leading provider of finance and military support to Kyiv.
Reaffirming Moscow’s long-standing demands, Medinsky told Russian state news agency TASS that “every inch” of Russian land would be returned to Russia — an apparent reference to Putin’s insistence that Ukraine surrender all of the Donbas.
Ukraine had hoped the Abu Dhabi talks would make progress towards a ceasefire on Black Sea grain shipments as a means of de-escalation, but Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, on a visit to Turkey, said Kyiv was still awaiting a Russian response.
FRONT LINE STATIC
Russian forces control about a fifth of Ukraine, much of it captured before the 2022 invasion, and their progress on the battlefield has slowed this year.
With the front line largely static, Moscow has been pounding Ukrainian cities and energy sites, while Ukraine has stepped up attacks on Russian oil refineries and other infrastructure.
Russian officials are calling for a broad agreement on European security architecture to be reached before tackling the specifics of the war.
Before its full-scale invasion in February 2022, Russia demanded the withdrawal of NATO forces from countries that joined the alliance after 1997, which the alliance rejected.
European officials say wider security talks should only come after a ceasefire, and that Russia should not be allowed to influence Europe’s security arrangements or be rewarded for starting the war.
Trump said last week the war was close to being settled in a “big beautiful agreement” that could include security guarantees for Europe. He has frequently predicted breakthroughs that have not materialised.
(Reporting by Reuters reporters in Abu Dhabi, Moscow, Kyiv and Dublin; Writing by Olena Harmash and Daniel Flynn; Editing by Timothy Heritage, Gareth Jones, Ron Popeski and Cynthia Osterman)

sources.title: Russia, Ukraine agree to major prisoner swap after U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi
sources.text:
Russia and Ukraine have agreed their biggest ever release of prisoners after two days of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, U.S. envoy Jared Kushner told reporters on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).
“One of the positives is that we agreed that we’re going to have the biggest humanitarian release of prisoners, and we’re going to finalise the numbers tomorrow,” he said.
Mr. Kushner and fellow U.S. mediator Steve Witkoff will travel to Moscow on Thursday (November 12, 2026) to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, and then to Dublin to debrief Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
The two sides have exchanged thousands of captured soldiers throughout the almost five-year war, started by Russia’s 2022 invasion.
But diplomatic talks have so far failed to move the two sides closer to an agreement to halt the fighting, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people.
The two days of conversations in Abu Dhabi appeared to fit that mould, with the prisoner exchange and agreement to carry on talking the only concrete outcomes mentioned by any side in post-talks press statements.
Russian envoy Vladimir Medinsky and Ukrainian negotiator Rustem Umerov also said a large scale prisoner exchange had been agreed, adding the numbers would be announced later.
Delegations from Moscow and Kyiv on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) held a second straight day of U.S.-brokered talks on ways of ending the war started by Russia's all-out invasion of Ukraine nearly five years ago.
The envoys met for four hours on Tuesday (November 10) in the capital of the United Arab Emirates, which was chosen as a neutral venue. The talks, mediated by U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and envoy Steve Witkoff, were due to conclude later Wednesday (November 11).
The context of the negotiations has changed since the last meeting in February in Geneva. The Trump administration has to reckon with Democrats, who could demand more support for Ukraine, taking over the U.S. Congress in January following the U.S. midterm elections.
Also, Russia's wartime economy is under heavy strain, and Ukraine is reeling from devastating aerial attacks on its power grid.
Mr. Umerov said that Wednesday (November 11) would begin with three-way talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States, with Kyiv's delegation meeting afterwards with European officials.
Moscow doesn't want European countries, which are concerned about Russia's conduct and broader intentions on the continent, involved in the direct negotiations.
However, representatives of European governments, the European Union and NATO were in Abu Dhabi and were consulting with the Ukrainian delegation, officials said.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Tuesday's (November 10) session was “constructive and quite substantive”.
The talks were largely about humanitarian issues, including possible prisoner exchanges and returning Ukrainian civilians in captivity, as well as children taken from the country, he said.
Security guarantees also were discussed, he said. However, Russia and Ukraine have shown no sign of a willingness to compromise on their demands.
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the meeting “very productive,” while cautioning that a breakthrough on stopping the war will take time.
The Abu Dhabi talks are being held against the backdrop of continued fighting on the front line, where little territory has changed hands this year.
Meanwhile, both countries are battering each other with long-range missiles and drones.
Overnight, Russia struck the southern Zaporizhzhia region and the eastern city of Kharkiv, wounding seven civilians and damaging property.
Russia's Defence Ministry said that air defences downed 627 Ukrainian drones overnight, 150 of them over the region around St. Petersburg, according to the regional Gov. Alexander Drozdenko.
He said the drones started a fire at the port of Ust-Luga, one of the main facilities for Russian oil exports, injuring three workers.
Published - November 11, 2026 04:21 pm IST

sources.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to major prisoner swap as peace talks end
sources.text:
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will separately meet Russia's Vladimir Putin and Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky on Thursday as they seek to seize "openings" from two days of talks in Abu Dhabi on ending the Ukraine war.
The two men will travel first to Moscow to meet the Russian president, before flying to Dublin – where Zelensky will attend European meetings – to debrief the Ukrainian leader.
Arriving in Ireland, Zelensky said there could be a "window of opportunity" to end Europe's worst conflict since World War II before 2027.
"What's important is that the Americans flew to Putin with specifics. I would very much like them to return to Dublin with specifics," he said, adding that, while he was still sceptical, "there is hope".
He also welcomed what he called "change in tone" from the US on the prospect of Europe's inclusion in the Washington-mediated talks, saying the "American side is treating it more positively, more warmly."
Read more Zelensky calls Ukraine-Russia talks 'constructive', Rubio wants Europe 'at the table'
European countries have been rattled by Russia pushing a review of the entire continent's security architecture, with the US also floating a new framework.
Moscow's chief negotiator said Wednesday the Kremlin aimed for a "new, modern Yalta" – referring to the 1945 conference in which Western leaders carved up Europe with the Soviet Union.
Some 50 European leaders are due to gather in the Irish capital Thursday, with the Abu Dhabi talks set to dominate the summit.
EU officials say there appears to have been little genuine progress towards peace and are adamant that Europe sees no need to discuss its broader security arrangement with Moscow before fighting stops.
NATO chief Mark Rutte however said Wednesday that the Abu Dhabi talks showed the US, Ukraine and Europe were "aligned and united".
'Biggest' prisoner exchange
Zelensky and the US have called on Europe to choose who will represent it at the talks – but European officials said they did not expect the leaders to take any decisions on naming a single envoy for any potential talks with the Kremlin.
After two days of talks in Abu Dhabi, the warring sides had agreed to a major prisoner exchange – the "biggest" ever, according to Kushner – though no side gave any figures.
Zelensky said Kyiv was waiting for a response from Moscow on a possible POW exchange that could be "1,000 for 1,000, maybe it will even come to 1,200".
He also said the parties went into "much greater detail" on the issue of security guarantees.
Ukrainian negotiator David Arakhamia said the talks had been tough, with Russia's delegation arriving with "strict directives", but they produced "good momentum" towards reaching a solution before the end of the year.
Kushner said the meeting with Putin would "go over what was discussed" in Abu Dhabi and to "try to make more progress on some of the issues that we discussed because we see some openings and some opportunities".
With Zelensky, the pair will "further explore some of the ideas that we came up with here today".
'New Yalta'
Kyiv's main negotiator Umerov said that there was "still a lot of difficult work ahead, but there are opportunities to continue the negotiation process".
Russia's delegation chief Vladimir Medinsky told reporters the "discussion will certainly continue".
But he questioned including Europe in the talks.
"We don't really understand what there is to talk about with them. We have not received a single peace initiative, not one concrete proposal from the European countries," he said.
Medinsky later told Russian TV that Moscow's aim is a "new, modern Yalta". Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky attends a bilateral press conference with Ireland's Taoiseach (Prime Minister) Micheal Martin at Government Buildings, in Dublin, Ireland, November 11, 2026.
Ukraine has warned against just that.
Kushner said seeking ways to "get the Europeans added to the format" would be on the agenda with Putin.
Officials from Britain, France, Germany and Italy, as well as NATO and the European Union travelled to Abu Dhabi for meetings on the sidelines.
Five years of war
Hundreds of thousands of people have been killed since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.
Millions more have fled the fighting in eastern and southern Ukraine, large swathes of which have been destroyed by relentless aerial bombardments.
Read more 'We call it war-life balance': Daryna's daily struggle to live, survive in wartime Ukraine
Russia is demanding Ukraine withdraw from parts of eastern Ukraine it still controls and wants a sweeping deal on "Europe's security architecture".
That is widely seen as a reference to Moscow's long-standing demands to push back the NATO military alliance in eastern Europe and end Western military support to Kyiv.
Kyiv says a ceasefire must come before any discussions on territory and has called for a direct meeting between Zelensky and Putin to discuss the biggest issues.
Putin has ruled that out.
(FRANCE 24 with AFP and Reuters)

sources.title: Russia, Ukraine Exchange 300 Prisoners Of War In Latest Swap
sources.text:
Russia, Ukraine Exchange 300 Prisoners Of War In Latest Swap
Zelenskyy said some of the Ukrainian soldiers freed by Russia were held for more than two years.
Got Question about the News?
Russia and Ukraine each said on Wednesday that 150 of their captured soldiers had been returned in the latest prisoner-of-war exchange between the two warring countries.
The two sides regularly swap prisoners of war in one of the only forms of cooperation between Kyiv and Moscow amid the nearly three-year war.

“Some of the guys had been in captivity for more than two years," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said in a post on social media.
Zelensky said 150 Ukrainian troops were being brought back, but did not mention handing over any Russian soldiers.
Russia’s defence ministry said it had swapped 150 captured Ukrainian troops for the return of 150 Russians held by Kyiv.
Its troops were undergoing medical checks in allied Belarus before returning to Russia, it said.
Zelensky posted photos showing the troops, some draped in Ukrainian flags, sitting in a bus on the way back to Ukraine.
Both sides said the deal was mediated by the United Arab Emirates, which has helped broker many such exchanges.
(This story has not been edited by News18 staff and is published from a syndicated news agency feed - AFP)

sources.title: U.S. brokers another Russia-Ukraine prisoner swap, but war continues as Putin sticks to demand for territory
sources.text:
U.S. brokers another Russia-Ukraine prisoner swap, but war continues as Putin sticks to demand for territory
Officials at U.S.-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine said Wednesday the two sides had agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war. Russia's demand to have its seizure of a huge swath of eastern Ukraine recognized as legitimate appeared to remain a key hurdle on the path to any breakthrough on a wider peace deal, however.
"One of the positives is we agreed that we're going to have the biggest humanitarian release of prisoners, which we're going to finalize the numbers tomorrow," Jared Kushner, President Trump's son-in-law and one of the two senior U.S. negotiators at the meetings, said after the two days of talks in Abu Dhabi ended.
Vladimir Medinsky, the head of the Russian delegation, and Rustem Umerov, who led Kyiv's delegation in Abu Dhabi, confirmed the planned exchange.
Hopes had been low for any major breakthroughs in the first meeting in nine months between the delegations. Russia and Ukraine have from time to time swapped prisoners during their nearly five-year war.
U.S. officials have said they are determined to revive Washington's peace efforts, which so far have failed to deliver significant results. Kushner said he and U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff would travel to Moscow Thursday to meet with President Vladimir Putin, then fly to Dublin to meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
Putin's senior aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters the U.S. envoys would arrive in Moscow Thursday morning and meet with Putin in the first half of the day.
Asked if there were plans to discuss any major new proposals, including on the dispute over Russia's claim to Ukrainian territory, or security guarantees for both countries, Ushakov said the results of the negotiations in Abu Dhabi were yet to be fully understood in Moscow, but he added that Russia believed Kushner and Witkoff were "bringing something with them."
Medinsky, speaking later to Russia's Vesti program, said Russia and Ukraine had moved closer to peace following the talks, but that much would still depend on the positions of Ukraine and the U.S., as well as "on whether Europe will come to its senses."
Russia has, throughout the war, tried to drive a wedge between the U.S. and its longtime NATO allies in Europe. European nations, along with Zelenskyy, have warned for years — long before Putin ordered the ongoing full-scale invasion — that capitulating to Russia would encourage the autocratic leader in the Kremlin to seek more territorial advances. President Trump, however, has pushed Kyiv to accept a deal that Zelenskyy and the Europeans believe would strongly favor Russia.
The context of the negotiations has changed since the last meeting in February in Geneva. The Trump administration has to reckon with Democrats, who could demand more support for Ukraine, taking over the U.S. Congress in January following the U.S. midterm elections.
Also, Russia's wartime economy is under heavy strain, and Ukraine is reeling from devastating aerial attacks on its power grid.
Umerov said Kyiv's delegation was expected to meet Wednesday with European officials, and Zelenskyy, on a visit to Denmark, acknowledged the prisoner exchange agreement and said after the delegations in Abu Dhabi "discussed their views on guaranteeing security," that it was "necessary that the first step be ending this war and providing security guarantees for Ukraine."
Zelenskyy said that after Kushner and Witkoff's visit to Moscow on Thursday, "we will coordinate our positions once again and determine what next steps are possible," confirming that the American envoys would head from Moscow to Dublin to meet again with Ukrainian officials.
"Ukraine's priority is to end the war as soon as possible with a dignified peace. We believe that Europe must be represented at every stage of real diplomacy," he said. "It is essential that the United States have a strong position and exert influence on the source of this war — that is Russia — so that Russia ends the war of its own making."
Moscow has said it doesn't want European countries, which are concerned about Russia's conduct and broader intentions on the continent, involved in the direct negotiations. However, representatives of European governments, the European Union and NATO were in Abu Dhabi and consulted with the Ukrainian delegation, officials said.
Zelenskyy said Tuesday's session was "constructive and quite substantive," but he balked at what he said had been a U.S. request for Ukraine to accept territorial concessions in exchange for security guarantees that fall short of his long-stated goal of Ukrainian NATO membership.
"No one believes that Putin will stop if we give up the Donbas," Zelenskyy said Tuesday, referring to eastern regions that have been largely, but not entirely occupied by Russia. "He might pause — but then he will return in a year, two years or five years. And who will be to blame then?"
"We discussed in detail the substance of security guarantees for Ukraine and the foundations for their long-term effectiveness," he said Tuesday, stressing that Ukraine needed "practical mechanisms to prevent any recurrence of the war."
This week's talks have largely focused on humanitarian issues, including the prisoner exchange and the potential return of Ukrainian civilians in captivity, as well as children taken from the country, Zelenskyy said.
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the Tuesday meeting "very productive," while cautioning that a breakthrough on stopping the war would take time.
Fighting on the front line in eastern Ukraine continues unabated, meanwhile. Little territory has changed hands this year, as both countries batter each other with long-range missiles and drones.
Overnight, Russia struck the southern Zaporizhzhia region and the eastern city of Kharkiv, wounding seven civilians and damaging property. Another strike hit a busy market in the southern region of Odesa, killing three people and injuring 11 others, according to regional governor Oleh Kiper.
Russia's Defense Ministry said air defenses downed 627 Ukrainian drones overnight, 150 of them over the region around St. Petersburg, according to the regional Gov. Alexander Drozdenko.
He said the drones started a fire at the port of Ust-Luga, one of the main facilities for Russian oil exports, injuring three workers.

sources.title: Russia, Ukraine agree large prisoner swap; talks end without breakthrough
sources.text:
Russia and Ukraine agreed a large exchange of prisoners of war, envoys said Wednesday as two days of US mediated talks concluded, but they announced no major breakthrough on ending the conflict that began after Moscow’s military operation in nearly five years ago.
Hopes had been low for any significant development in the first meeting in nine months between the delegations. Russia and Ukraine have from time to time swapped POWs but have remained far apart in their demands for accepting a peace settlement.
US officials say they are determined to revive Washington’s peace efforts that so far have failed to deliver significant results.
As well as postwar security guarantees for both countries, other key hurdles for negotiators are the fate of Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory and what role European countries will play in an eventual settlement.
The session was the first such meeting since February on Russia’s military operation, which analysts and humanitarian organisations say has killed hundreds of thousands of soldiers and thousands of civilians.
“One of the positives is we agreed that we’re going to have the biggest humanitarian release of prisoners, which we’re going to finalise the numbers tomorrow,” said Jared Kushner, US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, after the talks in Abu Dhabi ended.
Vladimir Medinsky, the head of the Russian delegation, and Rustem Umerov, who led Kyiv’s contingent, confirmed the planned exchange, though Medinsky noted that the agreement was “in principle.”
Kushner said he and US envoy Steve Witkoff will travel to Moscow on Thursday to meet with President Vladimir Putin, then fly to Dublin, Ireland, to meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
